A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PriVi dataset and recognition framework, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v3 additionally contains Appendices A-E. All supplied material supports comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, behavior-recognition and ablation results, including experiments across four benchmarks in Tables 2-5.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds predicted-box evaluation, label-efficiency experiments, class-level analyses and joint-pretraining results.

M1.justification: The V-JEPA backbone, loss and narrow attentive classifier remain unchanged. v3 adds optional procedural extensions: SAM3 supplies predicted boxes, with empty-box examples added during classifier training, and Appendix E evaluates joint PriVi/target-dataset pretraining instead of sequential adaptation.

E1.justification: The four benchmarks and 424-hour pretraining corpus are retained. v3 extends evaluation of the proposed method to ChimpACT without supplied ground-truth detections, changing its input requirements. Expanded source descriptions and revised species statistics do not establish that new training populations were added.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds UniFormerV2-B to the BaboonLand comparison, reporting 63.45 accuracy and 28.67 balanced accuracy. AlphaChimp was already compared in v1; v3 retains it in a separate predicted-detection comparison rather than introducing it as a new baseline. Most comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Additional experiments substantially expand the evaluation design: sequence-level training subsets of 10%, 25% and 50%, evaluation with predicted detections, a single-test-view control, and joint pretraining for 75k steps using a 50:50 data mixture. These are added protocols; newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct label-efficiency tests against X3D (Figure 5), a test-view ablation (Table 5), qualitative predictions and class-level error analyses (Figures 4 and 7), contamination screening (Appendix B), and joint-pretraining tests addressing catastrophic forgetting (Table 8). These substantially extend the original component and dataset-composition ablations.

E5.justification: Figure 5 introduces 95% confidence intervals estimated over three randomly sampled subsets per reduced training size. Appendix D newly discloses averaging AlphaChimp over five runs. Averaging five attentive classifiers was already stated in v1 and is retained; the PDFs do not establish an increase in that run count.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for label efficiency, predicted detections, individual classes and joint pretraining. Table 4 reports SAM3 plus PriVi/DaLP at 30.76 mAP versus AlphaChimp's retained 25.35. Existing V-JEPA baseline entries also change, including ChimpACT mAP from 30.85 to 36.33, while PriVi's 39.25 remains unchanged. Table 1 revises marmoset statistics and separately reports squirrel monkeys.

T1.justification: Equations 1-5 retain the same learning objective and classifier formulation. The token-matrix dimension ordering changes notation without introducing substantive mathematical reasoning. Neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 adds an explicit priority claim that this is the first demonstration of successful domain-level pretraining for video models, distinguishing it from target-dataset pretraining. It also newly claims that its curation pipeline uniquely requires neither seed datasets nor text captions. These substantially broaden the novelty positioning beyond v1's retained dataset, recognition and efficiency contributions.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges mixed PanAf500 accuracy effects and cross-dataset forgetting, discusses joint training's compute tradeoff, and proposes motion-feature and crop-related explanations for class-level behavior. The ground-truth-box limitation is removed following the added evaluation. However, Appendix E's claim of no performance reduction overstates Table 8: joint PanAf500 training lowers ChimpACT mAP from 38.75 to 37.93.

D1.justification: The new supplement documents source datasets, labeling rules, model identifiers, filtering thresholds, MLP training settings, contamination checks and baseline reproduction procedures. v3 also specifies the existing DaLP stage's 10k-step budget and test-data handling. Its abstract supplies a project URL and reports resource availability, replacing v1's release promise; the private subset remains withheld.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially reframes the work around domain-level versus dataset-level adaptation, adding connections to Gururangan et al.'s language-model adaptation and Mueller et al.'s primate pretraining work. It also introduces the seed/caption-free positioning against existing data engines. Additional references cover SAM3, UniFormerV2, ASBAR and the behavioral studies supplying R&O footage.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the introduction and contributions around the domain-level/dataset-level distinction, standardizes CID terminology to DaLP, moves detailed benchmark descriptions into Appendix C, and relocates adaptation procedures into the experimental setup. It reorganizes the results, expands technical explanations in Appendices A-E, compresses the conclusion and removes the future-work paragraph.

P2.justification: v3 adds an overview graphic, prediction examples, label-efficiency plots, a dataset-image gallery and class-level plots. It merges v1 Tables 2-3 into Table 2, reorganizes the benchmark table, separates predicted-detection results, and adds appendix tables. The architecture illustration and title/author layout are also revised.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves important evidentiary gaps: Figure 5 directly tests v1's label-efficiency claim, Table 4 evaluates operation without ground-truth boxes, and the supplement makes data curation and baseline comparisons substantially more reproducible. Contamination screening and forgetting analyses further strengthen scrutiny of the results. Some interpretations remain overstated, particularly complete avoidance of forgetting in Appendix E, but this limitation does not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and transparency.
